#54 v3: how often does a device-thread read of guest VRAM race a guest write? SUPERSEDES v2 (and v1) on ONE THING ONLY -- leg 6's statistic. Legs 1 to 5, the arms, the controls and every limit are carried forward unchanged from v2; this file restates them so it stands alone, and the wording of legs 1-5 is identical.

WHAT IS ALREADY LANDED WHEN THIS IS WRITTEN, said first so nobody has to work it out. Arm A run 1 (13ccda425a, result 1789301811-vram-race-probe-1217554) has landed: 60 gfps lines, gfps max 60 p90 59.0 median 32.5, G p10 16.79 ms, Tq median 627, mb_emitted 0, apk 88452c539d64. Both v1 arm-B runs have landed (ae0283fe2d, the MIS-PLACED bracket, retained as the negative control for the placement). Arm A run 2 is in flight and NO v2 arm-B run has landed. So leg 6's statistic below is registered before the arm it judges exists on one side and after one run on the other, and that is the honest position rather than a claim of purity.

WHY v3 EXISTS. v2 made the primary cost statistic the gfps LINE COUNT over a fixed 150 s soak -- guest frames rendered in fixed wall time. The performance lane's measurement retires that: absolute per-window counts vary 3-5x WITHIN a single run (`tossed` 1,434 -> 4,985), and a frames-in-fixed-time count is an average over the soak, so it carries the device's occupancy exactly the way a median does. Two Galleon soaks on one device, both gfps max 29 p90 29, had medians 27 and 17. A busy device would then read as a cost this instrument imposed. The cost leg must come off the CEILING.

WHY THE BARE CEILING IS ALSO NOT ENOUGH ON THIS TITLE, and this is set down before the arm rather than after it. DOA3 reaches the display cap: D: sits at 16.7 ms (59.9 Hz) and the landed runs give gfps max 60, 59, 59 with p90 59.0, 59.0, 56.6. A statistic pinned at the cap cannot move, so it cannot show a cost either -- it is insensitive by construction, not robust. The cap-free reading is the ceiling OF THE UNCAPPED PHASE.

LEG 6 -- COST. Statistic fixed here.
  primary: p90 and max of gfps over the pacing lines with gfps <= 50, and p10 of G ms over the same lines. The 50 is set by the display cap (59.9 Hz), not by the shape of any series: a frame the display limited is not measuring the build, and including those lines is what makes the bare ceiling insensitive. If fewer than 10 lines survive the filter on any run, leg 6 is NOT MEASURED on that run and says so.
  reported, advisory, no verdict reads them: bare p90/max gfps and p10 G over all lines (pinned at the cap); the gfps line count (an average, occupancy-sensitive, v2's retired primary); median gfps (occupancy, demonstrated).
  noise floor MEASURED, not assumed: two runs per arm, same ref, same title, same device, same --who. The floor is the within-arm spread. An arm with ONE run has no measured spread and leg 6 returns NOT MEASURED rather than a comparison -- v2's reader printed "ABOVE the floor" for a -2.5% delta against a floor of NaN, which is #64's missing control with a decimal point on it.
  decision rule: the probe's cost is below the noise floor if |delta p90 gfps(uncapped)| <= max(within-arm spread of the two arms) AND |delta p10 G(uncapped)| <= the same. Anything larger is reported as the cost in percent with both spreads beside it.
  expected: below the floor. The corrected probe scans only when texture_vram_gen bumped across a begin_pre_draw window; the mis-placed run measures 950 of 487,013 windows taking any scan at all, so the common path is one 32-bit compare per draw. The vertex site scans once per vertex-range copy, 32,847 of them per 150 s. But "read-only" is a claim about a bitmap's implementation and not a measurement, which is why this leg exists.
  AND EVERY RATE IS REPORTED AS A RATIO, never as a per-window count: Tr/tex_uploads, Tr/tex_windows, Vr/vtx_copies. Absolute counts varying 3-5x within one run is exactly why.

THE INSTRUMENT. Two device-thread reads of d->vram_ptr, each preceded by a test-and-CLEAR of the very dirty bits it then scans, which is what turns "written at some point since boot" into a WINDOW:
  Vr:raced/copies          sync_vertex_ram_buffer test-and-clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a range and then copies it out of guest memory. Clean on entry by construction; a bit set again when the copy returns is a guest store into it DURING the copy.
  Tr:raced/uploads/windows begin_pre_draw windows. pgraph_vk_poll_bound_textures consumes every bound texture's DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX bits at the top of the window and bumps texture_vram_gen when it finds any, so a bump means the guest had written a bound texture and we then read that memory; `raced` means the bits were set again by the time the window closed.
  Xd:                      the impossible row, leg 1.
No write side, deliberately: a per-page last-written stamp would be a store in every guest VRAM write, the position the +34.1% instrumentation occupied.

WHAT THIS MEASURES FOR THE SKEW LANE, SAID PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME MECHANISM IN DIFFERENT VOCABULARY. Asked directly whether the scan can distinguish "this read overlaps a region the guest wrote since we last synced": YES, and that is precisely what `tex_uploads` is. The poll's test-and-clear IS the sync point, so a texture_vram_gen bump across a window means exactly "the guest wrote this bound texture's pages since we last synced them, and we then read them". `tex_uploads/tex_windows` is therefore the rate at which a draw's texture read follows an unsynced guest write, and `Tr/tex_uploads` is the rate at which the guest was STILL writing when the read finished. In #44's vocabulary: tex_uploads counts the draws exposed to skew, Tr counts the subset where the skew was a torn read rather than a clean version substitution. Both are per-draw rates on a real title, which is the quantity the pfifo bound is trying to shrink. This lane does not touch pacing; nv2a.c and pfifo.c are the skew lane's and any overlap is reported to it rather than acted on.

ARMS. A = 13ccda425a (integration branch HEAD, no probe). B = e353735028 (A plus the probe, nothing else; 3c01fd73a0 adds only a prototype and is byte-identical). Title and device held fixed: Dead or Alive 3 on the THOR for the cost pair, whose attract loop renders real gameplay without needing input injection. Crimson Skies on the THOR as a second reading, because its attract FMV is per-frame dynamic VRAM traffic -- the workload #54 itself names as the one the test corpus cannot exercise. One --who across all of them so device_label cannot drift, which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.

LEG 1 -- THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW. Xd reads EXACTLY 0 on every run of arm B.
Xd counts a dirty bit observed to go from set to clear between two back-to-back scans of the same range with nothing between them but the probe's own arithmetic. The guest only ever SETS these bits, and the only code in this process that clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A or _NV2A_TEX is the vertex sync and check_texture_dirty, both on the thread already inside the call. The arithmetic forbids it.
The worlds in which it FAILS, none forced by the patch: page indices that straddle a DIRTY_MEMORY_BLOCK_SIZE boundary wrongly, so the second scan reads a different word than the first; an RCU blocks pointer that is not stable across a scan; or the pfifo and pgraph.vk.render threads running these paths concurrently after all -- render_thread.c's RCMD_FLUSH does call pgraph_vk_update_vertex_ram_buffer, and this probe assumes the requester waits on flush_complete. A non-zero Xd indicts the instrument, not the emulator, and every other leg is void until it is explained. (It read 0 on both v1 runs, over 999,103 windows and 66,142 copies, which is evidence for the arithmetic but not for the new window.)

LEG 2 -- THE PATH IS LIVE. tex_windows > 0, tex_uploads > 0 AND vtx_copies > 0 on every run of arm B, and tex_uploads > 5,000 per 150 s soak.
tex_uploads is the denominator leg 3 divides by and the one that matters: it was 950 and 964 under the wrong bracket, and a rate of zero over a denominator of 950 bounds nothing -- 3/950 is 3.2e-03, above leg 3's own 1e-04 threshold -- yet reads exactly like leg 3's decisive "closes on evidence" outcome. v2's leg 2 as first written ("tex_windows > 0") passed that run, which is why the threshold is here. A tex_uploads still in the hundreds means the window is still in the wrong place and legs 3, 4 and 5 are NOT MEASURED.
The discriminator between "window still misplaced" and "this title genuinely writes bound textures rarely": v2's tex_uploads against v1's 950/964 on the same title and device. v2 includes the poll's bumps and v1 did not, so v2 >> v1 means the window moved as intended; v2 ~= v1 means it did not.
A zero or thin denominator reads as "not measured", never as "zero races".

LEG 3 -- THE RATE, which is the measurement #54 needs.
Predicted: 1e-4 <= Tr/tex_uploads <= 3e-1 on Dead or Alive 3.
Not fitted from anything this arm produces. The lower bound is a claim that the window is hit at all in a game; the upper is set by #44, where the same race in a synthetic tight loop loses on 1 to 3 of 12 testifying swatches per run over 6 of 10 runs -- order 10% per upload under maximal pressure -- and a game re-binds far more textures than it re-uploads, so the game rate must sit below that.
The two decisive outcomes, declared before the number exists:
  Tr/tex_uploads effectively zero (Tr == 0 on every run, with leg 2 passing so the denominator is real, and 3/N below 1e-04 so the bound rules the rate out rather than merely not seeing it) -> the window is never hit in practice, the hazard is theoretical, and #54 CLOSES on evidence rather than on argument. This is the outcome #54's own text predicts under "incidental ordering elsewhere -- locks, syscalls, the PFIFO path itself -- may serialise enough in practice that the window is never hit."
  Tr/tex_uploads >= 1e-4 -> #54 gains a frequency, a call-site list and a target. It does NOT gain a licence for the blanket barrier: the +34.1% experiment already localised that cost to TCG code generation (renderer idle 27 -> 44 ms while frame time went 52 -> 70 ms), so the answer is targeted fences at the few sites a device thread reads guest memory.
A zero on a denominator whose 3/N bound sits ABOVE 1e-04 is a THIRD outcome and is reported as such: not measured finely enough to close the issue, and the fix is more soak time rather than a conclusion.
The failing world: the guest genuinely never writes a bound texture's page while the upload is reading it, because the pushbuffer handshake serialises them. Real, and nothing in this patch forces it either way -- the probe reads a bitmap the memory subsystem maintains whether the probe exists or not.

LEG 4 -- THE TEXTURE SITE RACES MORE THAN THE VERTEX SITE.
Predicted: Vr/vtx_copies < Tr/tex_uploads.
Mechanism: the vertex window is a memcpy of a few KB; the texture window is a poll, a convert, a swizzle and a staging copy of up to megabytes -- one to three orders of magnitude longer, and a race rate scales with the window.
The failing world is concrete: a title streaming dynamic vertex buffers rewrites them immediately before drawing from them far more often than it rewrites textures, which inverts the ordering. An inversion changes the target list for a narrow fix, and is a finding rather than a refutation.

LEG 5 -- WHETHER THE SAME INSTRUMENT MEASURES #44's SKEW.
Tr counts "a bound texture's dirty bits were consumed inside the window and set again by the time it closed", which is the guest writing the texture while the upload read it -- #44's resolved mechanism, the upload for draw N reading guest memory after the guest has begun writing iteration N+1 to the same address.
Predicted: Tr > 0 on at least one arm-B run.
The limit, stated in advance so it is not read into the result later. Tr is a FLOOR on #44's skew rate: if the guest COMPLETES iteration N+1's write before the poll clears the bits, the clear consumes that write, the upload reads a fully written successor, and nothing is set again -- #44's `cut == complete` case, invisible here. Page granularity cuts the other way: a write to the same 4 KiB page but a different byte counts, so Tr is an UPPER bound on byte-level overlap. Floor on version skew, ceiling on byte overlap; different quantities, and neither is "the rate at which frames are corrupted". `tex_uploads/tex_windows` is the broader and less ambiguous quantity for the skew lane -- see above -- because it needs no claim about what was in flight, only that the guest wrote between two syncs.

CONTROLS, not legs.
  mb_emitted must read 0 on the hakuX-build line in BOTH arms. Neither arm restores barriers; a non-zero value means the wrong ref was built. (Landed so far: 0 on all three.)
  Tq: (tex_dirty_queries) must be indistinguishable between the arms. The probe adds no test-and-clear and removes none, so if Tq moves, the probe has changed the path it is observing. (Landed: A 627, B 629 and 606.)
  device_label must read "thor" on every result. Four soaks across two handhelds with nothing recording which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.
  apk_sha must differ between the arms and agree within each arm. (Landed: A 88452c539d64, B(v1) b21ce5cf1c99.)

ASSERTIONS, recorded so they are not counted as falsifiers, because the code forces them: Tr <= tex_uploads <= tex_windows, and Vr <= vtx_copies.

WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT DECIDE. Whether a race it counts actually corrupted a frame. It counts windows, not wrong pixels, and a soak has no frame capture -- an exclusion already established on #54 which this instrument does not lift. It also cannot see the surface-upload read, deliberately uninstrumented: nothing on the device clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a surface range -- the vertex sync clears only its own ranges and update_surface_part's own scan is behind !tcg_enabled() -- so the bitmap is monotone there and a probe on it would report a plausible number with no time base in it.

FORM. The three arm-B v2 soaks were queued with --no-expect, correctly, because --expect was silently broken for soaks at the time: the binding block sat inside `if [ -n "$SUITES" ]`, so a soak recorded `expect` with an EMPTY `expect_sha` and the verdict would read UNBOUND. That is fixed now and any further soak on this issue uses --expect against this file. ab_compare's machine-readable slots are per-capture and a soak produces no captures, so the registered expect_counts are degenerate on purpose (better=0, worse=0, must_not_move '*' -- if ANY capture appears in either arm the request was mis-dispatched as a suites run and every leg is void). The legs are numbers read off the hakuX-perf line by docs/testing/vram_race_report.py; they are bound here by this file's content hash, which matters MORE for a soak than for a disc arm, not less: nothing computes a verdict, every reading is interpreted by hand, and the hash is what makes a leg quietly widened once the numbers arrive detectable.
